::: {.callout-note}
San Francisco is a prominent center of Autonomous Vehicle (AV) activity. Data describing AV activity in San Francisco, however, is spread across multiple sources, redacted from public reports, collected with insufficient detail, or in some cases not collected at all. Please see [Transparency](./transparency.html) for more information.
:::

::: {.column-body}
This dashboard provides insights into AV activity using publicly available data collected by the California Department of Motor Vehicles (California DMV), the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC), and the National Highway Transportation Safety Administration (NHTSA). Where possible, it focuses on San Francisco, but in many cases is limited to California statewide analysis. See Chapter 2 of the [AV Conceptual Permitting Framework](https://www.sfcta.org/reports/conceptual-safety-focused-av-permitting-framework) for more information about the regulatory roles of each agency, and the [Transparency](./transparency.html) section for more information about the data they collect.

Waymo is currently the only company with approval to provide paid passenger service from the CPUC in California. Cruise previously held a passenger service deployment permit. In addition to Waymo, Zoox holds a deployment permit with the California DMV, but does not yet have a CPUC deployment permit. Dozens of other companies hold DMV testing permits.
:::
